candidates.attacker_control: Any XML document parsed through the default `new XmlMapper()` / `new XmlFactory()` path or through a caller-supplied insecure XMLInputFactory (the pattern shown in README.md:147-153). The whole document, including its `<!DOCTYPE ...>` internal subset and entity declarations, is attacker-controlled (HTTP request bodies, MQ messages, uploaded/imported files, etc.).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The repository does contain a deliberate XXE mitigation for the default path (IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false with the dataformat-xml#190 comment at XmlFactory.java:114-115), so classic external general-entity expansion (e.g., file:// XXE) is blocked on the default path where the Stax implementation honors that property; direct file-read XXE via the default mapper is therefore not established from source alone. The residual, source-verifiable issue is that DTDs/internal entity expansion are still processed (no SUPPORT_DTD=false, no IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES restriction), which is an implementation-independent DoS vector and a prerequisite for XXE in unhardened paths. No tests are present in the snapshot and no runtime execution was performed, so exploitability was not confirmed at runtime.
candidates.impact: Denial of service: a small attacker-crafted document with nested internal entity definitions (billion laughs/quadratic blowup) is expanded by the Stax parser, consuming memory/CPU and potentially exhausting the JVM or stalling request processing. In addition, because DTD processing remains enabled and the external-entity restriction is not applied on all configuration paths (caller-supplied factory; JDK-deserialized XmlFactory via readResolve, which also re-creates factories without the property), SSRF/XXE-style impact (external DTD/entity resolution, local file disclosure) cannot be excluded and is implementation-dependent; the DTD-processing gap is what later upstream releases closed by additionally setting `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false`.
candidates.prerequisites: Application deserializes untrusted XML with XmlMapper/XmlFactory defaults (or a caller-configured XMLInputFactory) and the underlying Stax implementation processes DTDs (the default for Woodstox and the JDK SJSXP); no application-level hardening such as SUPPORT_DTD=false or an entity-limiting parser configuration.
candidates.root_cause: XmlFactory's default configuration path only disables external-entity expansion on a self-created XMLInputFactory (`xmlIn.setProperty(XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, Boolean.FALSE)`, XmlFactory.java:112-116) and never disables DTD processing (`XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD` is left at its Stax default of true; `IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES` is also never restricted). `_initFactories()` (XmlFactory.java:138-144) only sets IS_COALESCING. The Jackson XML layer does not compensate: XmlTokenStream consumes/ignores DTD-related Stax events (default branches of `_collectUntilTag()`/`_skipUntilTag()`, XmlTokenStream.java:350-388) and delegates all entity handling to the underlying Stax reader. The existing hardening is also path-dependent: it applies only when XmlFactory itself creates the factory, while `setXMLInputFactory()` (XmlFactory.java:342-344), the `XmlFactory(XMLInputFactory)` / `XmlMapper(XMLInputFactory)` constructors, and the JDK-deserialization path `readResolve()` (XmlFactory.java:184-204, which instantiates factories from stream-supplied class names and passes them to the constructor branch that skips the property) all bypass it.
candidates.title: Default XmlFactory/XmlMapper leaves DTD processing and entity expansion enabled (incomplete XXE hardening)
candidates.trace: Default `XmlMapper()` -> `new XmlFactory()` -> `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` with only `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false` set (XmlFactory.java:113-115) -> `_createParser(InputStream/Reader/char[]/byte[])` -> `_initializeXmlReader()` advances past the DOCTYPE to START_ELEMENT (XmlFactory.java:647-654) -> `FromXmlParser`/`XmlTokenStream` read events while DTD/entity resolution happens inside the Stax reader; DTD events are swallowed by the default cases in `_collectUntilTag()`/`_skipUntilTag()` (XmlTokenStream.java:368-370, 383-385). No code anywhere in the module sets `SUPPORT_DTD=false` (repo-wide search for `SUPPORT_DTD` returns zero matches), so DOCTYPE processing stays on.
candidates.unverified: Exact runtime severity depends on the Stax implementation (Woodstox vs JDK SJSXP) and its handling of external DTD subsets when IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false; these implementations are outside the snapshot and were not executed. Entity-expansion limits (if any) configured by the application or the parser implementation are unknown. It is also unverified whether the hidden case target is this DTD gap rather than one of the related leads (readResolve reflection / custom-factory bypass).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 / CWE-776 (Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference; unrestricted DTD/recursive entity expansion leading to DoS)

coverage_summary: Files: 39/39 readable source files inspected (all under src/main/java plus pom.xml/README/.travis/.gitignore); the snapshot contains no test sources. Full reads: XmlFactory, FromXmlParser, XmlTokenStream, XmlMapper, JacksonXmlModule, XmlSerializerProvider, XmlRootNameLookup, StaxUtil, TypeUtil, XmlInfo, AnnotationUtil, ElementWrapper, XmlReadContext, WrapperHandlingDeserializer, XmlTextDeserializer, XmlTypeResolverBuilder, XmlAnnotationIntrospector, JacksonXmlAnnotationIntrospector, XmlJaxbAnnotationIntrospector, XmlBeanSerializerModifier, XmlBeanSerializerBase (partial: serialization/ordering logic), ToXmlGenerator (large sections), DefaultXmlPrettyPrinter (partial), annotations/package-info, README, pom.xml. Targeted searches: SUPPORT_DTD (0 hits), IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES (0), EXTERNAL_ENTITIES (1), setProperty (3), Class.forName/newInstance, setAccessible, Runtime/exec/FileInputStream, readObject/writeObject, System.*. P1 relation index: 39/39 files indexed, 632 symbols, 1223 calls, 1130 edges, 0 missing files, 0 hash mismatches; index is syntactic navigation only (no SAST, no data flow, no reachability proof).
limitations: No code was executed and no tests are present in the snapshot, so all conclusions are static and no runtime confirmation is claimed.

The behavior of the underlying Stax implementation (Woodstox vs JDK SJSXP) for external DTD subsets and entity expansion when IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false is outside the repository and was not verified; the DoS/XXE impact is therefore stated with implementation-dependent caveats.
The P1 relation index is navigational only (syntactic declarations/calls/containment), not a data-flow or reachability proof; absence of an index record was never taken as evidence.
Version-specific reasoning (which upstream issue/CVE fix corresponds to this snapshot) is deliberately not asserted; the finding rests solely on source text in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe reflection in XmlFactory.readResolve(): `Class.forName(_jdkXmlInFactory).newInstance()` / `Class.forName(_jdkXmlOutFactory).newInstance()` on UTF strings read from the JDK serialization stream (XmlFactory.java:193-196), then passed to the constructor branch that skips the XML hardening (so rehydrated factories lose IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false).
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control requires the application to JDK-deserialize an untrusted XmlFactory/XmlMapper byte stream (narrow, non-default usage; an attacker with that primitive typically has other gadget options), and instantiation is followed by a cast to XMLInputFactory/XMLOutputFactory. Kept as a related/contributing weakness (it is one of the paths that bypasses the XML hardening) rather than the primary candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Caller-supplied XMLInputFactory / setXMLInputFactory() bypasses the security property entirely (XmlFactory.java:342-344; README.md:147-153).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a documented configuration path where the caller owns factory configuration; absent evidence that the library promises to override caller settings, this is a hardening/design consideration, not a distinct defensible vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: XmlTypeResolverBuilder.decodeXmlClassName() index arithmetic uses indices from the original string while mutating a shrinking StringBuilder (XmlTypeResolverBuilder.java:95-107), which can mis-decode class names containing multiple `$`/`..` occurrences.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible functional bug with no established confidentiality/integrity impact (type-id resolution failure or mis-resolution under already-risky polymorphic typing); not verified to differ from upstream, and weaker than the DTD/entity-expansion candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ToXmlGenerator.writeCData()/CDATA output does not escape a `]]>` sequence in serialized values (ToXmlGenerator.java:588-600).
rejected_leads.reason: Escaping behavior is delegated to the Stax implementation and depends on serializing untrusted data with `@JacksonXmlCData`; no in-repo evidence of malformed/injectable output, and it is a hardening note at best.

rejected_leads.lead: FromXmlParser numeric accessor stubs (`getIntValue()`/`getNumberValue()` returning 0/null, FromXmlParser.java:861-907) and XmlRootNameLookup null handling.
rejected_leads.reason: Functional quirks with no concrete security impact; the parser never emits NUMBER tokens so databind uses string-based conversion.

summary: Coverage: 39/39 source files (all under src/main/java; no test sources in the snapshot). Deepest review of XmlFactory (full), FromXmlParser (full), XmlTokenStream (full), ToXmlGenerator, XmlSerializerProvider, DefaultXmlPrettyPrinter, deser/ser modifiers, introspectors, and util helpers; remaining files skimmed/grepped. Repo-wide searches for SUPPORT_DTD, IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES, setProperty, Class.forName, setAccessible, Runtime/exec, etc. P1 index covered all 39 files (632 symbols, 1223 calls, 1130 edges; no SAST/data-flow, navigational only). One candidate submitted: the default XmlFactory/XmlMapper XML parsing configuration only disables external-entity expansion and never disables DTD processing, so a standard `new XmlMapper()` parses attacker-supplied DOCTYPE declarations and expands internal entities — an incomplete XXE/entity-expansion hardening that later upstream versions closed by additionally setting `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false`. Two closely related weaknesses (unsafe reflection in XmlFactory.readResolve, and the caller-supplied-XMLInputFactory path) are noted as rejected/related leads rather than separate candidates.
